correctness.rationale: Exact side-facet inequalities w_j dot s ± cz/h < 0 give both pole and equatorial conditions. The regular-normal net implies a pole-illuminating direction must have |z|/h > ||s|| while averaging consecutive equatorial facet constraints gives |z|/h<||s|| for an equatorial direction. Thus pole mass separates from equatorial mass; each horizontal direction illuminates <=m=floor((n-1)/2) equatorial vertices, with all m-consecutive blocks attainable. Cyclic cover lower/upper bounds give I=2+ceil(n/m), I*=2+n/m. Exact optimality equations sum_{r=0}^{m-1} x_{k-r}=1 imply x_k=x_{k-m}; gcd(n,m) yields constant x=1/m except n mod4=2 with alternating masses a+b=2/m. The unequal-height pentagon has tilted directions (-w_j,-11/10) that illuminate upper pole plus two adjacent equator points; strict radical inequality 19sqrt(5)>41 and a lower pole/equator separation prove I=4 and I*=7/2. Independent numerical strict facet checks for all five tilted witnesses and exact radical comparison corroborated the example.
